title: Title
pointer: 标题 → “Machine Learning for Time Series Data” → 左下角 Tutor 信息（轻点即离开）
review_note_zh: 开场：课程定位，把“数据结构—特征—模型—评估”串成一条线。
script_en: Welcome to Tutorial Six. Today we look at machine learning for time series data, and connect the data structures, the features, the models, and the evaluation choices that make a time-series project trustworthy.

title: Tutorial outline
pointer: 依次指 1 Data、4 Models、5 Evaluation、6 Group project；最后停在 6。
review_note_zh: 路线图：先数据/任务/特征，再模型/评估，最后落到 group project。
script_en: Here is the route. We begin with data: what changes when every observation has a time stamp. Then we define tasks and build temporal features. Next, models: from logistic regression to sequence encoders and ARIMA. Evaluation comes next, because a time-series model is only useful if it respects the prediction cutoff. Finally, I introduce the group project. The project is a two-week learning-platform pause prediction task. Keep that task in mind; it will make the later choices concrete.

title: Time series data: adding a time dimension
pointer: 先指左侧表格，再指 patient A 的折线图，最后指底部 “Observations indexed by time”。
review_note_zh: 时间维度：同样是一个病人，按小时展开后，值的顺序和间隔也变成信息。
script_en: Tabular data gives one row per patient: age, heart rate, and so on. A time series keeps the same patient but adds an axis. Here patient A has heart rate at hours zero to three: 80, 84, 96, 108. The values matter, but so do their order and the interval between them. That sounds simple, yet it changes everything downstream. We can no longer shuffle rows freely, and a single summary may hide the pattern we care about. The rest of this tutorial is about making those choices deliberately.

title: Data structures: rows, time steps and channels
pointer: 先框 Z ∈ R^{N×D} 表格，再框右侧 X ∈ R^{N×L×F} 张量，最后停在 “100 × 24 × 3”。
review_note_zh: 两种数据形状：二维表 vs 三维序列张量；重点检查 time 在哪一维。
script_en: These are the two shapes you will use all the time. On the left, a table: N examples and D features per example. One row is one patient. On the right, a sequence tensor: N examples, L time steps, and F channels. One patient is an L by F block. Our synthetic ICU cohort has one hundred patients, twenty-four hourly steps, and three vital signs, so the tensor is one hundred by twenty-four by three. With one vital sign, F equals one, and many libraries store it as N by L. When you load data, check which axis is time. Most bugs start with a shape that looks plausible but has time in the wrong place.

title: Time series tasks: prediction and detection
pointer: 按行移动：Forecasting → Classification → Sequence labeling → Anomaly detection；最后指 “Output axes”。
review_note_zh: 四类任务的输出形状不同：horizon/channel、单概率、逐时刻状态、逐时刻异常分数。
script_en: All four tasks share the same input: observed histories, N by L by F. What differs is the output. Forecasting predicts the next H hours for K signals, so the output has a horizon and a channel axis. Classification predicts whether a future event occurs, one probability per example. Sequence labeling predicts a state for every observed hour, so the output keeps the time axis. Anomaly detection returns a score per hour. Before modeling, write down the output shape. It tells you whether you need one prediction per patient, per hour, or per future step, and it rules out many accidental mistakes.

title: Characteristics: order and temporal patterns
pointer: 依次框 Trend、Daily rhythm、Sudden change 三个小图；最后指 “Temporal order”。
review_note_zh: 三种常见形态：趋势、日周期、突变；共同点是 order 不能打乱。
script_en: Time series have patterns that tabular rows do not. The left panel shows a trend, a sustained rise. The middle panel shows a daily rhythm, a repeating seasonal shape. The right panel shows a sudden change, a shock. Order is the common thread: which reading came first? If you shuffle these points, the trend and the rhythm disappear. So before you engineer features, look at the series. Ask whether the pattern is a trend, a cycle, a shock, or dependence on recent values. That diagnosis suggests which features and which validation scheme will be honest.

title: Modeling approach: from sequences to features
pointer: 沿箭头 Hourly readings → Temporal features → Classifier → Class probability；最后指下面的问题。
review_note_zh: 传统路线：先把 history 压成特征，再用 logistic/trees；问题是“哪个特征能区分上升和下降”。
script_en: One practical approach is to compress the history into features, then use a standard classifier. Hourly readings become a small set of numbers, such as the mean, the latest value, and the change. A logistic model or a tree ensemble maps those features to a probability. This is often the strongest baseline, and it is easy to explain. The key question is on the slide: which feature distinguishes a rising series from a falling one? If your features cannot tell those two apart, no classifier can recover the information.

title: Feature engineering: level, recency and change
pointer: 先框 A/B 两行原始序列，再指 Mean 列的 90/90，再指 Latest value 的 120/60，最后指 Change 的 +60/−60。
review_note_zh: 同一个均值 90 可能对应完全相反的走势；latest 和 change 补回方向。
script_en: Here is why one summary is not enough. Patient A rises from 60 to 120; patient B falls from 120 to 60. Both have mean 90. The mean captures the overall level, but it loses the order. The latest value separates them: 120 versus 60. The change, latest minus earliest, is plus 60 versus minus 60. That is the direction and size of the movement. In practice, give the model several complementary views: level, recency, and change. Later, add variability and extremes. The model can then combine them, but you must make sure the information is actually present.

title: Feature engineering: temporal summaries
pointer: 按行轻点：Overall level、Recency、Change、Variability、Extremes、Context。
review_note_zh: 可直接落地的特征清单；先做小而可解释的一组，再看 validation 是否值得加。
script_en: These are useful summaries to compute over the observed window. Overall level: the mean heart rate. Recency: time since the last measurement, and the latest value. Change: the recent six-hour mean minus the previous six-hour mean. Variability: the standard deviation, or hour-to-hour differences. Extremes: maximum heart rate, minimum blood pressure. Context: age and admission type. Notice that these are not model-specific. They are a language for describing a history. Build a small, interpretable set first, then check whether more features improve validation performance.

title: Task definition: input window and target
pointer: 先框左侧 observed 0–23，再指 Prediction cutoff 竖线，再框右侧 outcome 24–29，最后指 Cohort。
review_note_zh: 把 input window、cutoff、target window、cohort 固定下来；这是后面所有比较的前提。
script_en: Now define the prediction problem precisely. We observe vitals from hour zero to hour twenty-three. The prediction cutoff is the end of hour twenty-three. The target is sepsis onset during hours twenty-four to twenty-nine. The cohort is patients who do not already have sepsis at the cutoff. This is a synthetic teaching example, not a clinical definition. The picture prevents a common mistake: using information from after the cutoff. The input window, the target window, and the cohort definition must all be fixed before you look at performance. If you change them later, you are effectively solving a different problem. Write them down, and use the same definition for every model you compare.

title: Preprocessing: where gaps come from
pointer: 先指 A/B/C 三类 gap 标签，再框 Patient A 图中的阴影缺口，最后指底部三条定义。
review_note_zh: 缺口有三种来源：没测、漏记、时间不规则；missing 不等于 0。
script_en: Real clinical data are full of gaps, and the reason for a gap matters. Not measured means no reading or test was ordered. The absence itself can be informative, because monitoring decisions are not random. A charting gap means the value exists but was not entered, so check whether the gap follows a pattern, such as nights or weekends. Irregular timing means readings arrive at event times, not on a fixed grid. Patient A shows a long gap around hours six to twelve. If we treat that gap as a zero, we invent a dramatic drop that never happened. Missing is not zero.

title: Preprocessing: filling one gap
pointer: 依次框 LOCF、Mean/median、Linear interpolation、Missing indicator 四个小图；最后指 “Keep the trace”。
review_note_zh: 四种补缺策略各有偏差；推荐保留 was_missing 和距上次测量的时间。
script_en: There are several ways to fill a gap, and each has a failure mode. Last value carried forward keeps the last level, but it invents a flat run that can hide a real change. Mean or median is simple and stable, but it erases the within-window pattern. Linear interpolation is smooth for short gaps, but it assumes a straight path across long ones. A better default is to keep the trace: add a missing-value indicator and the time since the last measured value. Then the model knows that the value is imputed, and how old the information is. Choose the fill method on validation data, not on the test set. And never fill using future values.

title: Preprocessing: irregular timing to a grid
pointer: 先框左上 “Irregular readings, 4-hour bins”，再指阴影 empty bin，再框右侧 daily grid，最后指底部三条规则。
review_note_zh: event log 的空 bin = 0；measurement 的空 bin = unknown；这个区别会改变特征含义。
script_en: Irregular readings need a grid. For vitals, an hourly grid is natural; for the project, one row per day. Bins are half-open, so each event belongs to exactly one bin. Then aggregate: count, sum, last, mean, max, and time since the last event. The empty-bin rule is crucial. In an event log, an empty day means zero clicks, so fill it with zero. For a measurement, an empty bin means unknown, so keep it missing. The bottom of the slide shows the difference: the four-hour bin with no reading is not a measured value of zero. This one distinction, zero versus unknown, changes the meaning of the feature and the model that can learn from it.

title: Preprocessing in pandas
pointer: 先指左侧 daily grid 代码（pivot_table / reindex），再指右侧 hourly grid 代码（date_range / reindex / ffill / interpolate），最后指 “Development data”。
review_note_zh: 把上一页的规则落到 pandas；强调 imputation 只在 train/validation 上探索。
script_en: Here is the same logic in pandas. On the left, events become a daily grid. A pivot table puts sample id on the rows and day on the columns, sums clicks, and fills an empty day with zero. Re-indexing makes sure every day from zero to twenty-eight exists. On the right, readings become an hourly grid. A date range creates the full index, re-indexing introduces missing values for absent hours, forward fill carries the last value forward for at most two hours, and interpolation fills short gaps for at most three hours. The missing indicator is a separate column, not a replacement. Development data means explore these choices on train and validation, and keep the test set independent. The test set is not a place to tune imputation.

title: Feature engineering in Python
pointer: 先指 mean/max 两行，再指 last_6h / previous_6h / change 三行，最后框底部的 “Can we use hour 24?” 问题。
review_note_zh: 用代码构造 level/recency/change；强调 hour 24 在 cutoff 之后，是 leakage。
script_en: This code builds the feature table. One row per patient, one column per hour. Mean and maximum are straightforward. The last six-hour mean and the previous six-hour mean average the two blocks, and change is their difference. The companion notebook contains the same code with saved outputs. Then the question at the bottom: can we use hour twenty-four? No. Hour twenty-four is after the cutoff. It is not available at prediction time, so it is leakage, even if it improves validation. Before you add a feature, ask: would this value exist at the moment the prediction is made? If not, leave it out.

title: Classifiers: logistic regression and trees
pointer: 先框左侧 logistic 公式，再框右侧 tree-based 文本，最后指 “First baseline”。
review_note_zh: 特征做好后就是标准分类器；先用 constant probability 做 baseline。
script_en: With a feature table, standard classifiers apply. Logistic regression computes a linear score and passes it through a sigmoid, so the output is a probability. Tree-based methods, such as a random forest or gradient boosting, can capture nonlinear rules and interactions among the summaries. Neither is automatically better. Always start with a baseline: predict the training event rate for everyone. If a model cannot beat that baseline on validation log loss, the extra complexity is not earning its place. And use the same features and the same split when you compare.

title: Sequence models: learning a representation
pointer: 沿箭头 Hourly vitals → Temporal encoder → Representation → Task head；最后指 “Training objective”。
review_note_zh: sequence model = encoder 学表示 + task head 做任务；不展开具体网络。
script_en: Instead of hand-building features, a sequence model learns a representation. An encoder, g with parameters theta, reads the hourly vitals and produces either a single representation vector per patient, h, or a representation for every time step, H. A task head then maps that representation to the required output: a forecast, a class, a label sequence, or an anomaly score. Training uses a suitable objective, such as forecast error, classification loss, or an anomaly-learning objective. The important idea is the separation: the encoder learns temporal structure, and the head answers the question. You can reuse the encoder for a different task if the input history is the same.

title: RNN: recurrent memory
pointer: 沿 x1 → h1 → h2 → … → hL → Task head 移动；最后指 “Limitation”。
review_note_zh: RNN 用 hidden state 记历史；只讲直觉和梯度问题，不推导公式。
script_en: The simplest sequence encoder is a recurrent network. At each hour it combines the current input with the previous hidden state through a hyperbolic tangent nonlinearity. The hidden state is the memory of the sequence so far. The limitation is practical: on long sequences, gradients can vanish or explode, so the network may forget distant information. That motivates gated architectures. We will not derive the gradients here; just recognize the failure mode and the reason for the next slide.

title: GRU: gated memory
pointer: 先指左侧 GRU cell 流程，再指 Reset gate、Update gate，最后指 LSTM 三行。
review_note_zh: GRU/LSTM 只用 gate 控制记忆；不要求学生会写公式。
script_en: A gated recurrent unit, or G R U, adds gates to the recurrent cell. The reset gate controls how much past information is used in the candidate state. The update gate balances the old state against the new candidate. A long short-term memory model, L S T M, takes a related approach but keeps a separate cell state. You do not need the equations today. The practical message is that gating gives the model a way to keep information over longer spans and to forget what is no longer relevant. For the project, these are options to try, not requirements.

title: Transformer: attention across time
pointer: 先框四个 hour token，再框 Self-attention + time encoding 条带，最后指 “Time order”。
review_note_zh: attention 让不同时刻互相看；只需理解 Q/K/V 直觉和 positional encoding。
script_en: A transformer takes a different route. Self-attention lets each hour look at other hours in the window and decide what to combine. The formula on the slide is the standard attention operation. Intuitively, a query says what to look for, a key says what is available, and a value is the content that gets combined. Because attention alone has no notion of order, we add positional or time encodings. For time series, the window is short enough that this can work well, but it needs more data and more compute than the simpler baselines.

title: Attention masks: observed vs. future inputs
pointer: 按行移动：Whole window → Alerting hour by hour → Forecasting → Padding。
review_note_zh: mask 决定模型能看哪里；它编码了 prediction-time 的信息边界。
script_en: Masks decide what the model is allowed to see. For a whole observed window, bidirectional attention is fine: every observed hour can see every other observed hour. For an alerting task, we usually want causal masking, so each hour sees only its past and present. For forecasting, we train autoregressively with shifted targets and causal masking. For variable-length sequences, padding must be masked so the model does not attend to fake positions. The mask is not a detail; it encodes the prediction-time information boundary. If the mask is wrong, the model can look into the future.

title: Forecasting: ARIMA (p, d, q) in pictures
pointer: 沿 Observed levels → Difference d times → AR(p)+MA(q) → Restore levels；再指 last p values / last q surprises；最后指 Example (1,1,1)。
review_note_zh: ARIMA 只讲流程直觉：差分→AR/MA→还原；不展开估计和定阶。
script_en: Now a short detour into classical forecasting. ARIMA is a family of models for a single series. The picture shows the logic. Start with the observed levels. Difference the series d times to remove a trend and stabilize the mean. Fit an autoregressive part and a moving-average part to the differenced values. The AR part uses the last p values; the MA part uses the last q surprises, or errors. Then restore the levels to get the forecast. For example, with p, d, q equal to one, one, one, we predict the next change from the last change and the last surprise. We will not cover estimation or order search; just recognize the structure.

title: Forecasting: what differencing does
pointer: 依次框 d=0、d=1、d=2 三个面板；最后指底部三行解释。
review_note_zh: 差分的目的是把“水平”变成“变化”；d 不是越大越好。
script_en: Differencing is the key idea, and this slide shows why. With d equal to zero, we model the level directly. A constant mean misses the drift, and the lag-one autocorrelation stays near one. With d equal to one, we model the change. The drift becomes a stable mean, and the autocorrelation drops to about zero. With d equal to two, we model changes of changes; here that adds unnecessary noise, and the autocorrelation becomes negative. So d is not a knob to maximize. It is a choice about what you want to model: levels, changes, or changes of changes. Check the differenced series before fitting.

title: Forecasting: ARIMA and its variants
pointer: 按行移动：AR/MA/ARMA → ARIMA → SARIMA → ARIMAX/SARIMAX；最后指底部 seasonal lag 图。
review_note_zh: 把 SARIMA/ARIMAX 当成 ARIMA 的扩展；知道有这些东西即可。
script_en: The variants extend the same idea. AR, MA, and ARMA use no differencing, which is appropriate for a stable series. ARIMA adds differencing for a drifting level. Seasonal ARIMA, or SARIMA, adds seasonal orders, P, D, Q, and a seasonal period s; for hourly data with a daily cycle, s is twenty-four. ARIMA with external predictors, sometimes called ARIMAX, adds known inputs such as a calendar or schedule. The seasonal lag picture at the bottom shows the idea: yesterday at the same hour, the previous hour, and the current hour. That is enough background for this tutorial; you will not be asked to tune ARIMA orders today.

title: Model comparison: assumptions and trade-offs
pointer: 按行移动 constant → logistic → trees → RNN/GRU → transformer；最后框 “Fair comparison”。
review_note_zh: 模型没有绝对优劣；fair comparison 要同病人、同 window、同 label、同 metric。
script_en: Here is the comparison we want you to carry away. A constant probability is the first reference. Logistic regression uses explicit summaries and is easy to audit. Tree ensembles capture interactions among summaries, but can overfit and can produce poorly calibrated probabilities. Recurrent networks and gated recurrent units learn memory from hourly vitals; check window length, tuning, and variability across runs. Transformers use attention across hours; check position encodings, data size, and compute. The last row is the most important: a fair comparison uses the same patients, the same input window, the same labels, and the same metric. Otherwise you are comparing experimental setups, not models.

title: Validation: development splits and a final test
pointer: 先沿 Train → Validation → Test 三个框移动，再指 “Choose the question”“Combine if needed”“Develop freely”“Freeze, then test”。
review_note_zh: 三份数据分工明确；按病人 group、按时间 split，最后 refit 后只测一次 test。
script_en: Validation is where time-series projects usually fail. We need three parts: train, validation, and test. Train fits candidates. Validation is for exploring, comparing, and tuning. Test is the final evaluation. The split must respect the prediction question. For new patients, group by patient, so the same person does not appear in both train and test. For future admissions, split by time. If you need both, enforce group and time separation. You may develop freely on train and validation: choose features, revise the split, inspect errors. But once you freeze the pipeline, refit on train plus validation, and apply that frozen pipeline to test once. That is the sequence that gives you an honest final number.

title: Data leakage: three boundaries to protect
pointer: 依次指 Prediction cutoff、Evaluation unit、Final test；最后指 “Validation is development”。
review_note_zh: 三条边界：cutoff 前可用、按人/时间分组、test 完全不参与开发。
script_en: Leakage has three boundaries. First, the prediction cutoff: every input must be available when the prediction is made. A diagnosis first recorded after hour twenty-three is not a valid input. Second, the evaluation unit: keep related records together when evaluating unseen people. Hourly rows from one patient, or repeat stays from one person, are the same grouping problem. Third, the final test: keep test statistics, labels, and feedback out of development. Fitting a scaler on train plus test is a classic mistake. Finally, remember that validation is development. Using validation to improve a model is expected, but its score can become optimistic. That is why the final test must stay untouched.

title: Evaluation: log loss
review_note_zh: log loss 惩罚“自信地错”；用三个数值建立 scale。
script_en: Log loss measures probability quality. The formula averages the negative log likelihood of the observed labels. The table makes the scale concrete. A septic patient predicted at 0.60 contributes 0.511. The same patient predicted at 0.90 contributes 0.105, a much smaller loss. A patient without sepsis predicted at 0.90 contributes 2.303, because being confidently wrong is expensive. This asymmetry is the point: log loss rewards calibrated probabilities and punishes overconfidence. It is the metric to use when the probability itself matters, not just the ranking.

title: Evaluation: ranking, calibration and errors
pointer: 按行移动 Log loss → Ranking → Calibration → Decision errors → Slices。
review_note_zh: 除 log loss 外还要看 ranking、calibration、threshold 后的 precision/recall 和 subgroup。
script_en: Log loss is not the only view. Ranking measures whether positives score above negatives; ROC AUC is the common summary, and PR AUC, the area under the precision-recall curve, is more informative when positives are rare. Calibration asks whether a predicted twenty percent risk corresponds to about twenty observed events. Decision errors, precision and recall at a chosen threshold, tell you what happens when you act on the model. Slices check performance by age group, ward, or admission period. A model can look good overall and fail a subgroup. Report more than one view, and choose the primary metric before you compare models.

title: Summary: two ways to represent a history
pointer: 先框左侧 Temporal features 分支，再框右侧 Learned representation 分支，最后指底部 task-specific output。
review_note_zh: 两条路线：手工特征+标准模型 vs encoder+task head；最后都落到任务输出。
script_en: Here is the summary in one picture. There are two ways to represent a history. On the left, temporal features plus a standard model: regression, classification, or anomaly scoring. On the right, a learned representation: an encoder plus a task head. Both end in a task-specific output: a forecast, a class, a state sequence, or an anomaly score. The choice is not about fashion. It is about data size, interpretability, and how much temporal structure you need to learn. Start simple, then justify complexity with validation evidence.

title: Group project: predict a two-week pause
pointer: 先框 Input days 0–28，再指 cutoff，再框 Outcome days 29–42，最后指 Output 和 Example/History tables。
review_note_zh: 项目定义：输入 0–28 天，预测 29–42 天零点击；cutoff 是第 28 天结束。
script_en: Now the group project. You will predict a two-week learning-platform pause. The input is days zero to twenty-eight: enrollment, learning activity, and eligible past assessments. The outcome is days twenty-nine to forty-two. If a student has no clicks in that window, the label is one; any clicks means zero. The prediction cutoff is the end of day twenty-eight. One example is one student in one module presentation. The output is the probability of zero clicks. train.csv is labeled; test.csv is unlabeled. The VLE events Parquet file gives clicks by day and type. The past assessments Parquet file gives past submissions. Your job is to build a history for each example without using anything after the cutoff. The project is deliberately open-ended; the brief and data instructions live on Moodle and Kaggle.

title: Group project: file formats and loading
pointer: 按行移动 CSV → Parquet → JSON/JSONL → Pickle；最后框底部读取代码。
review_note_zh: 格式取舍：CSV 通用、Parquet 适合事件表、JSONL 流式、Pickle 只做本地缓存。
script_en: Use the right file format for the job. CSV is portable and easy to inspect, but it is slow and types are inferred. Parquet is typed, compressed, and columnar, which suits the event tables; it needs pyarrow. JSON is convenient for small nested records, and JSON Lines stores one record per line, which is easier to stream. Pickle is fast as a local cache, but it is unsafe to load from untrusted sources and fragile across versions. The code shows the project files: read train.csv, read the Parquet columns you need, read past assessments, and read the sample submission. Read only the columns you need; the event table can be large.

title: Group project: starting questions
pointer: 按行移动 Representation → Baseline → Validation → Improvement；最后指 Instructions。
review_note_zh: 五个起点问题：表示、baseline、validation、改进、官方说明；强调按 cutoff 和 split 解释设计。
script_en: These questions are your starting point. Representation: which parts of the history might matter? Baseline: what is the simplest probability prediction you can make? Validation: how will you handle later presentations and repeated students? Improvement: does a change improve validation log loss, not just training accuracy? Instructions: read the project brief on Moodle and the data and submission instructions on Kaggle. Treat these as design questions, not a recipe. A good project explains why a feature is available at the cutoff, why the split is fair, and why the metric matches the decision.

pointer: 依次指 Course project、Features and splits、Data and formats、Sequence models、Forecasting background；最后停在 Contact。
review_note_zh: 延伸阅读和联系方式；提醒从 notebook 开始，不必今天读完所有资料。

You do not need all of them today. Pick the one that matches your project. The companion notebook is the place to start. Contact details are on the slide. Thank you, and good luck with the project.
